label: Diffuse_Large_B_Cell_Lymphoma_NOS
query: Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma NOS
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), NOS is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
- Typically presents with rapidly enlarging lymph nodes or extranodal sites.
- Immunophenotype is characterized by CD19, CD20 positivity.
- Key histological feature: diffuse proliferation of large B-cells.
- Important to use the Hans algorithm for classification into germinal center B-cell-like (GCB) and activated B-cell-like (ABC) subtypes.

## Terminology
- Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, Not Otherwise Specified (NOS).
- Synonyms include "DLBCL, NOS".

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Diffuse effacement of architecture by medium or large lymphoid cells with centroblastic or immunoblastic morphology.
  - Positive for mature B-cell markers, such as CD19, CD20, TdT-negative.
  - High Ki-67 index, but less than 95%.
  - Exclude high-grade B-cell lymphomas with MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements.
- **Desirable:**
  - Absence of MYC rearrangements.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Genetic abnormalities often involve BCL2, BCL6, and MYC genes.
- May arise de novo or as a transformation from a lower-grade lymphoma.

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Primarily affects adults, incidence increases with age.
- **Presentation:**
  - Typically presents with rapidly enlarging masses in lymph nodes or extranodal sites.
- **Prognosis:**
  - Prognostic factors include IPI score, cell-of-origin subtype (GCB vs. ABC), and genetic features.

## Macroscopic
- Lesions are typically enlarged lymph nodes or extranodal masses.
- Tumor masses are greyish-white and can contain necrosis.

## Microscopic
- Features diffuse growth pattern of large atypical B-cells.
  - Centroblastic, immunoblastic, and anaplastic morphologies may be present.
- **Images:**
  - ![A tonsil showing centroblastic cytology.](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/PEDS/18960.jpg)
  - ![Cytological features in DLBCL.](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/lymphomadiffuseklairmont02.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **IHC:**
  - CD19, CD20 positive.
  - High Ki-67 index.
  - Hans algorithm to classify into GCB or ABC subtype.
- **Molecular:**
  - Rule out MYC, BCL2, BCL6 rearrangements.
  - GCB subtype may show BCL6 rearrangements; ABC may show MYD88 mutations.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Burkitt Lymphoma:**
  - Uniformly high Ki-67 index (> 95%).
  - Presence of starry sky pattern.
  - MYC translocation.
- **Follicular Lymphoma:**
  - BCL2 rearrangement.
  - Nodular growth pattern.
- **Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma, NOS:**
  - Negative for B-cell markers like CD20.
  - Shows a more polymorphic T-cell infiltrate.
- **Primary Effusion Lymphoma:**
  - Associated with HHV8.
  - Presents as body cavity effusions without a solid tumor mass.
- **KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma:**
  - Associated with KSHV/HHV8, often in patients with immunodeficiency.
  - Displays plasmablastic, immunoblastic, or anaplastic morphology.
  - Immunostaining for LANA (KSHV/HHV8) and IgM positivity.

For more information, you can visit [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/PEDS/Diffuse_Large_B_Cell_Lymphoma_Nos.html) and [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/lymphomadiffuse.html).

This section focuses on PMBCL and its differential diagnosis with these lymphomas, as the other diseases and systemic lymphomas involving the thymus, the commonest of which is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS), are discussed elsewhere in this volume. PMBCL is a mature aggressive B-cell lymphoma of putative thymic B-cell origin, arising in the anterior mediastinum. It represents 2–3% of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Familial clustering of PMBCL cases has been reported based on shared genetic mutations. PMBCL occurs predominantly in young adults in their third decade, with a female predominance of 2:1, but it can also occur in children. cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS Section: microscopic PTCL-NOS can cause complete or partial effacement of the lymph node architecture. In most cases the pattern is diffuse, with medium to large pleomorphic cells. Less common cases with pleomorphic small and large cells are also described [[WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Haematolymphoid tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2024. (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11). https://publications.iarc.who.int/637.]]. Small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, and histiocytes are present in the background. Haemophagocytosis can occasionally be detected. Residual atrophic follicles can be present. Clustered and scattered epithelioid histiocytes are frequently seen. cards.title: KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma definition: Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus / human herpesvirus 8 (KSHV/HHV8)-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a large B-cell lymphoma consistently associated with KSHV/HHV8, in general arising in patients with profound immunodeficiency, but it may occur in non-immunocompromised patients. The tumour cells morphologically resemble plasmablasts or immunoblasts and have abundant cytoplasmic IgM. related_terminology: Acceptable: HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS. Not recommended: large B-cell lymphoma arising in HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease (obsolete). essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: presentation with primary nodal and/or splenic involvement; effacement of architecture by large blasts / transformed B cells with generally plasmablastic, immunoblastic, or anaplastic morphology; positive immunostaining for LANA (KSHV/HHV8) and IgM. Desirable: absence of immunoglobulin somatic hypermutations; EBER in situ hybridization (usually negative but can be positive in some cases).

cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS (PTCL-NOS) is a heterogeneous category of mature T-cell lymphomas that do not correspond to any of the specifically defined entities of mature T-cell lymphomas. related_terminology: Not recommended: T-cell lymphoma NOS; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, pleomorphic small cell; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, pleomorphic medium and large cell; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, large cell; Lennert lymphoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a mass-forming clonal T-cell proliferation with a variable histological appearance; exclusion of immunodeficiency-associated lymphoproliferative disorders other than lymphoma; exclusion of specific T-cell lymphomas (i.e. lymphoblastic lymphoma, anaplastic large cell lymphoma, EBV-associated lymphoma/lymphoproliferation, and cutaneous T-cell lymphomas). Desirable: involvement of more than one site; aberrant T-cell phenotype confirming neoplastic nature.

cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS) is a heterogeneous category of nodal and extranodal mature T-cell lymphomas that cannot be assigned to a specific PTCL entity, consisting of a broad cytomorphological spectrum of medium to large lymphoid cells with variable degrees of pleomorphism.

cards.title: Splenic B-cell lymphoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Splenic B-cell lymphoma definition: Primary splenic B-cell lymphomas (PSLs) are subtypes of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and include the primary splenic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which in the fifth edition of the WHO classification of haematolymphoid tumours has been renamed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS), and four small B-cell lymphomas: hairy cell leukaemia (HCL), splenic marginal zone lymphoma (SMZL), splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma (SDRPL), and splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli (SBLPN).

cards.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS) is a neoplasm of mature blastic B cells with a diffuse growth pattern. DLBCL-NOS encompasses all cases that do not belong to a specific diagnostic category of large B-cell lymphomas. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: architectural effacement by a diffuse proliferation of medium or large lymphoid cells with centroblastic or immunoblastic morphology; mature B-cell immunophenotype, TdT-negative; high Ki-67 index (but < 95%). Desirable: absence of MYC rearrangements; genetic testing, if relevant.

cards.title: DLBCL, NOS — Prognostic factors
cards.excerpt:
Unfavorable prognostic features:
Clinical: ↑ age, ↑ LDH, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) ≥ 2, Ann Arbor stage III / IV, extranodal disease, bulky disease (J Clin Oncol 2010;28:2373, Blood 2014;123:837)
Cell of origin status (Blood 2004;103:275):
Activated B cell subtype (~40%) and germinal center B cell subtype (~60%) associated with 5 year progression free survival rates of 40 - 50% versus 70 - 80%, respectively
MYC translocation (Blood 2015;126:2466)
Double expresser status: immunohistochemical coexpression of MYC (≥ 40% tumor cells) and BCL2 (≥ 50% tumor cells) in the absence of co-occurring MYC and BCL2 rearrangements

cards.title: DLBCL, NOS — DLBCL involving the kidney
cards.excerpt:
Frozen section description
Large atypical lymphoid cells with a diffuse growth pattern consistent with a large cell lymphoma can be appreciated on frozen sections; however, ancillary immunophenotypic and cytogenetic studies are required to establish B cell lineage and further differentiate specific DLBCL subtypes

cards.title: DLBCL, NOS — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:
Partial or complete effacement of normal tissue architecture by a diffuse infiltrate of large (or occasionally medium size) atypical B lymphoid cells with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Large is defined as nucleus size ≥ histiocyte nucleus or > 2 lymphocyte nuclei

cards.excerpt:

Cytologic evaluation can identify large atypical lymphoid cells with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli, consistent with a large cell lymphoma; however, classification as DLBCL, NOS requires immunophenotypic and cytogenetic studies

cards.title: DLBCL, NOS — Germinal center B cell (GCB) subtype: CD10+ or CD10- / BCL6+ / MUM1-
cards.excerpt:
Non-GCB subtype (classifier that encompasses ABC subtype and unclassifiable cases by GEP): CD10- / BCL6- or CD10- / BCL6+ / MUM1+
Double expresser status (30% of DLBCL, NOS):
Positive staining for BCL2 (> 50% tumor cells) and MYC (> 40% tumor cells) in the absence of underlying chromosomal rearrangements (double expresser) is associated with increased risk of CNS relapse and inferior survival (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2515)
If MYC and BCL2 rearrangements confirmed by FISH, classified as high grade B cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (also known as double hit DLBCL)

cards.title: DLBCL / high grade B cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements — Prognostic factors
cards.excerpt:
Relatively low response rate with R-CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone, plus the monoclonal antibody rituximab) with short overall survival (4.5 - 18.5 months), prompting investigation of alternative therapeutic approaches (J Clin Oncol 2010;28:3360, Blood 2015;126:2466)
MYC partner: MYC / IG translocation may have a worse outcome compared to non-IG partner in some studies although this remains an area of investigation (Blood 2015;126:2466, Haematologica 2014;99:726)
Tumor morphology (may warrant further study, per WHO): majority of double hit lymphomas have DLBCL morphology and can be indistinguishable morphologically

cards.title: KSHV / HHV8 positive diffuse large B cell lymphoma — Essential features
cards.excerpt:
Usually arises in association with multicentric Castleman disease (MCD) and HIV infection
Morphologically similar to plasmablasts but correspond to naïve IgM producing B cell without somatic hypermutations
Sheets of HHV8 latency associated nuclear antigen (LANA1) positive plasmablasts efface lymph node architecture
Atypical cells are strongly positive for cytoplasmic IgM with lambda light chain restriction and negative for EBV encoded small RNA (EBER)

cards.title: KSHV / HHV8 positive diffuse large B cell lymphoma — Epidemiology
cards.excerpt:
Rare disease with overall frequency of 0.1% (Leuk Lymphoma 2018;59:1375)
Median age is 47 years (range 39 - 66); M:F = 3.3:1 (Pathology 2020;52:53)
Usually arises in association with HHV8 positive multicentric Castleman disease (MCD) and HIV (15 times higher risk) (Blood 2002;99:2331)
